E12 — FET Small-Signal II: Source Follower, Common Gate, E-MOSFET, Loading, Cascades and Design (T10, Week 8 second half)

Why this matters in the exam: Week 8 is the last block of examinable transistor content before op-amps, and the final is expected to weight FETs and Weeks 6–10 heavily. WS9 Q5–9 are the only practice set for this material and they have no official solutions, so they are a likely source of final-exam questions (the practice test reused workshop questions word for word). Expect a “find , , ” question (6–8 marks), a cascade “find each stage gain and ” question (6–10 marks), and possibly a short design part (“choose for a gain of 10”). E11 covered for JFETs and the common-source amplifiers. This pack finishes the job.

1. The core ideas

1.1 One model for every FET

Every FET in this course uses the same ac model: an open circuit from gate to source, a current source from drain to source, and in parallel with it. Only the formula for changes.

1.3 The configurations in this pack

Source follower (common drain). Input on the gate, output on the source, drain at ac ground.

is positive (in phase) and always less than 1. is low (a few hundred ohms), which is why it is used as a buffer or output stage. With a load, replace by in .

Common gate. Input on the source, gate at ac ground (directly, or through a bypassed divider as in WS9 Fig. 5), output on the drain.

is positive. is low (hundreds of ohms), so a CG stage loads its source heavily.

E-MOSFET drain-feedback amplifier. from drain to gate, source grounded.

is not . Miller-type feedback divides by about , so 10 MΩ becomes about 2 MΩ.

E-MOSFET voltage divider. Same as the JFET case: , , .

1.4 Loading: and (slides 51–53)

  • No-load gain is the biggest gain. A load lowers it, and a source resistance lowers it again.
  • : put in parallel with whatever resistor the output is taken across ( for CS and CG, for the follower).
  • : a voltage divider at the input: , so .
  • For FET CS and CD stages is megohms, so hardly matters. For a CG stage is hundreds of ohms, so matters a lot.

2. The method

2.0 Recognise the configuration

Find where the signal goes in and where it comes out.

Signal in Signal out AC-grounded terminal Configuration
Gate Drain Source (or unbypassed) Common source (E11)
Gate Source Drain (tied to ) Source follower
Source Drain Gate (direct or bypass cap) Common gate
Gate, with drain to gate Drain Source Drain feedback

In WS9 Fig. 5 the input line hops over the bias wire and lands on the source. The gate sits on the 91 MΩ/11 MΩ divider with a bypass capacitor, so it is ac ground. That is a common gate.

4. Traps that cost marks

  • Using for the drain-feedback amplifier. It is , several times smaller.
  • Using for a source follower. It is , usually dominated by (a few hundred ohms).
  • Putting a minus sign on CG or follower gains, or dropping it on CS gains. Week 8 slide 40 writes for a CS D-MOSFET stage; it should be −8.05.
  • Ignoring for a CG stage. is comparable to , so half the signal can be lost (WS9 Q6).
  • Misreading Sedra’s . If W/L is asked, and the course is (WS9 Q8).
  • Rounding inside a cascade. Rounding to changes from 38.9 to 38.4 (slide 59). Carry 3–4 s.f.
  • Using the slide 53 for the unbypassed self-bias stage. That entry contradicts slide 48, which gives ; with an ideal current source () nothing reduces below . Use .
  • Not rechecking dc after a design. A larger for more gain can push below (ohmic region). Then the design fails.

7. Add to your open-book reference sheet

FET SMALL-SIGNAL II (Week 8 second half)
gm: JFET/D-MOS gm0 = 2IDSS/|VP|, gm = gm0(1 - VGSQ/VP)
    E-MOS gm = 2k(VGSQ - VGS(Th)),  k = ID(on)/(VGS(on)-VGS(Th))^2
    Any:  gm = 2ID/|VGS - Voff|      rd = 1/gos  (not given -> infinity)
Sedra: Vov = VGS - Vt, ID = 1/2 unCox (W/L) Vov^2, gm = unCox(W/L)Vov = 2ID/Vov
    course k = 1/2 unCox (W/L).  If W/L is asked, given "k" = unCox.
CONFIG        Zi                       Zo               Av
CS (byp/VD)   RG or R1||R2             RD||rd           -gm(RD||rd)
CS unbyp RS   RG                       ~RD              -gmRD/(1+gmRS+(RD+RS)/rd)
Src follower  RG                       rd||RS||1/gm     gm(rd||RS)/(1+gm(rd||RS))  <1, in phase
Common gate   RS||(rd+RD)/(1+gm rd)    RD||rd           (gmRD+RD/rd)/(1+RD/rd) ~ gmRD, in phase
              ~ RS||1/gm
Drain fdbk    (RF+rd||RD)/(1+gm(rd||RD)) RF||rd||RD     -gm(RF||rd||RD) ~ -gmRD
              ~ RF/(1+gmRD)
LOADING: put RL in parallel with output resistor (RD, or RS for follower).
         Avs = Zi/(Zi+Rsig) * AvL   (big effect only for CG)
CASCADE: AvT = Av1*Av2, Zi = Zi1, Zo = Zo(last), RL1 = Zi2; Vo = AvT*Vi.
         Don't round stage gains before multiplying.
DESIGN:  RD||rd = |Av|/gm -> RD = 1/(gm/|Av| - 1/rd); standard value; recheck
         VDS > VGS - VP (saturation).
Sedra quick: CG matched -> 1/gm = Rsig, Gv = 1/2 gmRD; follower Ro = 1/gm,
         Av = RL/(RL+1/gm); ID = gm Vov/2; W/L = gm/(unCox Vov).
